key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXenes are not chemically inert in perovskite precursor inks: I2/polyiodides rapidly damage them, PbI2 causes slower oxidation, and MAI can passivate and stabilize the surface.
engineering_relevance: MXene performance in halide perovskite devices depends strongly on precursor chemistry and mixing order, so ink formulation and processing sequence must be controlled to preserve flake integrity and tune interfaces.
method: XPS to track surface chemistry and oxidation states
DFT to explain adsorption and reaction mechanisms
Comparison of MXene exposure to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components
evidence_signal: The paper combines detailed XPS measurements with DFT calculations to link observed MXene surface evolution to specific precursor species and addition order.
watch_item: Device fabrication using MXenes in perovskite inks may fail or vary if iodine-rich species are present or if precursor mixing order is not strictly controlled.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
